question.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the major depressive episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

info.persona: James Pugh, a structured and sociable 80-year-old, they blend methodical volunteering, budget-tight living, and a love for Midwestern food and history into a life marked by quiet generosity, occasional over-salted casseroles, and a firm belief that community service keeps the mind sharp.
info.professional_persona: James Pugh, a retired carpenter who now serves as the senior volunteer coordinator at the local senior center, exemplifies an organized, methodical approach, and they channel it into meticulous budgeting, event planning, and hands-on mentorship of younger volunteers while still delighting in occasional woodworking projects around the community.
info.cultural_background: James grew up in post‑war Broadview, Illinois, within a working‑class white family of German and Irish ancestry. The Midwestern values of practicality, modesty, and community service shaped his upbringing. He attended a local public school and later took some college courses before entering the workforce. His generation experienced the Korean War era, and he completed a brief stint in the U.S. Army, which reinforced his sense of discipline and civic duty. Religion has played a steady role in his life, with regular involvement in a Protestant (Methodist) church that emphasizes fellowship and charitable work. These cultural influences have contributed to his organized, reliable, and sociable character.
info.hobbies_and_interests: James enjoys a mix of social and solitary pursuits that reflect his outgoing yet organized nature. He participates in a local bowling league and a bridge club where he meets friends weekly. Gardening remains a favorite pastime, and he belongs to the community garden committee. He reads historical nonfiction and biographies, especially about the World War II era and Midwestern development. Cooking classic Midwestern dishes for family gatherings and church socials brings him joy. He also volunteers at the food pantry, attends Chicago Cubs games when possible, and takes regular walks with his spouse through the parks of Broadview.
info.sports_persona: James Pugh, a devoted Chicago Cubs fan and active member of a local bowling league, follows the Cubs' season religiously, attends summer games whenever possible, and they balance these passions with regular walks in Broadview parks to stay fit.
info.arts_persona: James Pugh, an avid lover of Midwestern folk music, frequently listens to John Prine and Gillian Welch, flips through WWII biographies, and they admire Grant Wood's paintings at the regional art museum.
info.travel_persona: James Pugh, an intentional weekend traveler, prefers driving to historic Midwest sites such as the Pullman National Monument and the Wisconsin family cabin, plans each trip with a printed itinerary, and they pack a garden-grown salad for the road.
info.culinary_persona: James Pugh, a confident home cook, delights in preparing classic Midwestern dishes like chicken pot pie, meatloaf, and corn casserole using fresh garden tomatoes, sweet corn, and rye flour, and they tend to over-salt their soups when reminiscing about family recipes.

info.persona: Josephine Manning blends a quiet curiosity for technology with a disciplined, community‑oriented mindset, balancing meticulous 3‑D printing projects and yoga sessions while they occasionally hoard stray coffee sleeves as tiny reminders of daily accomplishments.
info.professional_persona: Josephine Manning, a mechanical‑electrical engineering technician in Central Florida, leverages CAD, prototyping, and data analysis expertise while applying their organized, methodical approach and quiet curiosity to deliver reliable, sustainable product solutions for aerospace and renewable energy projects.
info.cultural_background: Josephine grew up in a suburban community in Central Florida, absorbing a blend of Southern hospitality and the multicultural vibrancy of the Orlando area. Raised in a middle‑class family that emphasized education, community service, and modest, practical living, she was encouraged to pursue curiosity‑driven learning while valuing reliability and cooperation. Her upbringing included regular family trips to local parks, the Kennedy Space Center, and community events, fostering an appreciation for space exploration, environmental stewardship, and inclusive collaboration within her predominantly white, yet diverse, Floridian context.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her free time, Josephine enjoys solitary activities that stimulate her curiosity and provide a sense of accomplishment, such as building scale models, 3D printing custom parts, and solving complex puzzles. She is an avid reader of science fiction and non‑fiction books on emerging technologies, and she frequently visits local nature trails for quiet hikes. She also practices yoga and light gardening to maintain balance and mental resilience. Occasionally, she joins small groups for board‑game evenings or volunteers at community STEM outreach events, where she can share her knowledge in a supportive setting.
info.sports_persona: Josephine Manning enjoys low‑impact fitness, joining the Orlando Track Club for weekend 5K runs, cheering on the Orlando Magic during the basketball season, and occasionally playing pick‑up ultimate frisbee with friends at Lake Eola, while their disciplined yoga practice keeps their body balanced.
info.arts_persona: Josephine Manning reads sci‑fi authors like Liu Cixin and attends local performances of the Orlando Philharmonic Orchestra featuring composers such as Philip Glass, while their own 3‑D printed miniatures serve as tangible tributes to the intricate sculptures of Anish Kapoor.
info.travel_persona: Josephine Manning prefers meticulously planned trips that blend exploration and sustainability, having road‑tripped through the Florida Keys to witness coral restoration projects, and dreaming of a future adventure to Iceland’s volcanic landscapes to study geothermal energy firsthand, while they keep a travel journal filled with sketches and technical notes.
info.culinary_persona: Josephine Manning enjoys cooking Mediterranean‑inspired meals, skillfully preparing a quinoa‑tabbouleh with fresh basil, feta, and lemon zest, while they also indulge in occasional Southern‑style fried green tomatoes during family gatherings, and never pass up a perfectly roasted cinnamon‑spiced sweet potato.

info.persona: John Hanoman is a diligent physician who channels anxiety into meticulous preventive care, escapes stress with solitary hikes and heritage cooking, and navigates life with a blend of structured ambition and lovable disorganization.
info.professional_persona: John Hanoman, a board‑certified internal medicine physician with a talent for streamlining patient workflows, leverages bilingual fluency and telehealth expertise to deliver preventive care while juggling a love of structure and occasional disorganization that sometimes leads to missed non‑urgent admin tasks.
info.cultural_background: John is a second‑generation Indonesian‑American raised in Fremont, California, a city with a large Southeast Asian diaspora. His parents immigrated from Indonesia in the early 1990s, instilling in him the language, customs, and communal values of his heritage. He grew up celebrating Idul Fitri, Hari Kemerdekaan, and family gatherings centered on satay and rendang, while also navigating the multicultural environment of the Bay Area. The cultural emphasis on harmony, respect for elders, and community service permeates his cooperative and considerate demeanor, and he remains actively involved in local Indonesian cultural organizations.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside the clinic, John gravitates toward solitary, low‑stress activities that nurture his well‑being. He enjoys reading medical research and philosophy, practicing mindfulness meditation to manage worry, and exploring the rolling hills of nearby parks on spontaneous hikes. Cooking traditional Indonesian dishes for a few close friends lets him stay connected to his heritage while sharing hospitality. He also volunteers at community health fairs, captures nature scenes through photography, and occasionally joins small‑group board game nights, preferring flexible, informal gatherings over rigid schedules.
info.sports_persona: John Hanoman follows the San Francisco Giants and the Golden State Warriors on game days, joins the Bay Area Hiking Club for weekend treks in the rolling hills, and occasionally participates in local pickup basketball games, balancing a love for low‑intensity outdoor activity with occasional team sports.
info.arts_persona: John Hanoman finds solace in photographing sunrise landscapes reminiscent of Ansel Adams, listens to the minimalist piano works of Ludovico Einaudi and folk melodies by Sufjan Stevens, and enjoys binge‑watching arthouse films by directors like Bong Joon‑ho during quiet evenings.
info.travel_persona: John Hanoman has explored the misty Redwood forests, trekked the ancient temples of Kyoto, and plans a future adventure to the fjords of Norway, favoring spontaneous itineraries that blend scenic hikes with cultural immersion yet staying within a modest travel budget.
info.culinary_persona: John Hanoman delights in preparing traditional dishes from their heritage for close friends, mastering the balance of aromatic spices, coconut milk, and freshly ground lemongrass, while also experimenting with quinoa‑based salads and sustainably sourced seafood to keep the menu diverse and health‑focused.
